record.paper_title: Causal Machine Learning: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Offline reinforcement learning learns policies from fixed observational trajectories without online experimentation, so the data can contain hidden confounding from unknown behavior policies or environments. How can such observational offline-RL data be deconfounded before or during policy learning?

evidence.quote: Deconfounding Offline RL: Whenever we aim to learn policies from an offline dataset without access to observed policy or the environment, this dataset likely includes confounding biases.
As we have seen throughout this section, a significant motivation for using causality for RL is to deconfound observed data, i.e., transform it so that confounding biases are removed.
We believe that deconfounding observational data is under-explored in pure offline RL settings, and only a few works have addressed this setup [256].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the offline reinforcement learning setting in which a learner is given a fixed dataset of trajectories D = {(s_t^i, a_t^i, r_t^i, s_{t+1}^i)} drawn from one or more unknown behavior policies acting in an unknown (possibly partially observed) Markov decision process. Assume that there exist unobserved variables U (hidden confounders) that simultaneously influence the actions a_t taken in the data and the observed rewards r_t and/or transitions s_{t+1}, so that the empirical conditional distribution P_D(r_t, s_{t+1} | s_t, a_t) does not equal the interventional distribution P(r_t, s_{t+1} | s_t, do(a_t)). The behavior policy that generated the data and the structural mechanism of the environment are not available, and no online interaction with the environment is permitted.

Develop a general methodology for "deconfounding" such offline reinforcement-learning data. Concretely:

1. Specify identifiability conditions (structural-causal-model assumptions, auxiliary variables, or qualitative constraints on U) under which the interventional transition/reward distribution P(r_t, s_{t+1} | s_t, do(a_t)), or equivalently the value of an arbitrary target policy π, can be consistently estimated from D alone.

2. Provide an algorithmic procedure that, either as a preprocessing step on D or jointly with policy optimization, produces an estimator of an optimal policy π* whose value under the true interventional environment converges to that of the optimal policy as |D| → ∞ under the stated assumptions.

3. When point identification fails, characterize the resulting partial identification region and design a policy-learning procedure with provable guarantees (e.g., regret or worst-case value bounds) over this region.

State and prove the corresponding consistency and/or sample-complexity guarantees.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is an active and only partially addressed research direction. A handful of works (e.g., deconfounding actor–critic for observational RL, causal deep RL using observational data, and "Delphic" offline RL under nonidentifiable hidden confounding) propose specific methods and uncertainty quantifications, but no general, broadly applicable solution with full identifiability theory and end-to-end guarantees has been established. The problem remains open in its general form.

status_evidence.title: Deconfounding Reinforcement Learning in Observational Settings
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes a deconfounding variant of actor-critic for RL with hidden confounders in observational data.
status_evidence.claim: Early targeted method exists, but limited in scope.

status_evidence.title: Delphic Offline Reinforcement Learning under Nonidentifiable Hidden Confounding
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces 'delphic uncertainty' to address nonidentifiable hidden confounding in offline RL.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work explicitly states hidden confounding in offline RL is widely overlooked and only partially handled.

status_evidence.title: Causal Deep Reinforcement Learning Using Observational Data
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes causal deep RL methods using observational data with confounding.
status_evidence.claim: Method-specific advances exist; general problem remains open.
